title: Agencies cutting salary and the early Nazarro pay scale
summary: After the Nazarro split agencies wanted to cut his pay; he recalls the original $100 a week and Nazarro's refusal to pay $125.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: and you're not getting much work, is that correct? After the lawsuit with Nazzaro you weren't getting much work?
How do you account for that?
Well, they want to cut the salary, don't want to give me the money.
The agencies that you worked with which was Joe Glaser --
They were trying to get you for much less than even Nazzaro got you for?
They couldn't do that because I didn't have no contract. Understand? Oh, then there was another point to the contract which you didn't get cleared up

concerning Nazzaro. You can clear it up right here if you want to. I told you the salary was supposed to be when we went back to Louisville to sign up with Nazzaro, the salary was supposed to be $100 a week, it was $90 and $100 and $125. All right? We got to $90 and $100, when we got $125 that's when he wanted to refuse to pay. That's when I started to go with another agency in Chicago and the other agency booked us in a place and he wanted to come raise sane and I said, well, you had a chance, you didn't book us and you wouldn't pay the money. So what do you want us to do, get somebody that's going to be able to pay us the money. This man is going to pay more money.
